logline: A wheelchair-bound K-pop fan time-travels to her idol's high-school years and races to prevent his death while untangling the consequences of rewriting the past.

renewal.note: No Season 2 announced; tvN has not renewed the series as of June 2026. K-drama limited runs rarely continue.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 8.5 and a MyDramaList score in the 9.1-9.2 range reflect genuine cross-border fandom; the time-travel mechanics frustrate some critics but the lead chemistry and emotional pacing drive an unusually high completion rate.

seasons.review_body: Lovely Runner landed as a breakout K-drama of the first half of 2024, turning Byeon Woo-seok into a major regional hit and elevating Kim Hye-yoon as one of the standout contenders. The time-travel scaffold is familiar, but the series runs it with enough emotional precision and comic lightness to keep plot-logic stretches from derailing momentum. Viewership and discussion repeatedly point to lead chemistry, along with the show’s ability to make its stakes feel genuinely personal despite the genre machinery. Western trade coverage was limited, with momentum largely sustained by stronger fan-driven conversation. The back half tests some viewers with pacing slack and time-loop repetition, while the prevailing read is that the emotional payoff still lands.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Im Sol, a wheelchair-bound K-pop fan, time-travels to 2008 and finds herself standing next to her idol Ryu Sun-jae as a teenager. The premise is outrageous; the execution is warm and fast-moving, and Byeon Woo-seok's performance as a teenage idol who doesn't know he's being saved signals immediately that the show has something real underneath its fantasy machinery.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Im Sol realising she is standing in the past and making the decision to stay - the show's thesis delivered in a single wordless beat.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 7
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The midpoint sharpens the time-travel paradox - every change Im Sol makes creates new dangers she couldn't anticipate. The show shifts gear from comedy to something more anxious, and the leads' chemistry is carrying real emotional weight by now rather than just comic energy.
episode_reviews.the_moment: A change in the timeline that Im Sol thought would fix things visibly making them worse - the episode that turned the fandom from delighted to devastated.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 13
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Sun-jae begins to understand what Im Sol has been doing and why, and the show shifts the emotional register from dramatic irony to mutual recognition. The back half’s time-loop repetition is felt most clearly in this episode, where it underscores the growing patience.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Sun-jae putting together Im Sol's behaviour across the timeline and the look on his face when the picture becomes clear.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 16
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale resolves the temporal loop with emotional precision rather than mechanical plot logic, which is why the MyDramaList score stayed above 9.1. PureWow noted the show's chemistry and emotional pacing as the reasons for its unusually high completion rate, and the finale is the culmination of both.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final scene across time - the show paying off its central promise in a way that is simultaneously predictable and genuinely moving.
